intro: You are about to enter the Zeugma Mosaic Museum in Gaziantep province, opened in 2011. It is the largest mosaic museum in the world, and every floor here has a story: these mosaics were rescued from Zeugma before the Birecik dam flooded the city.
history: In 2000 the Birecik dam began to fill, and the water was set to drown most of Zeugma. An international rescue excavation lifted the floor mosaics out of the villas. Here, the museum lays them out following the plan of the rooms they came from — so you do not walk across the mosaics, you walk through the houses.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Gypsy Girl, the Dionysus and Ariadne mosaic and the Poseidon hall. Seek out the Statue of Mars too, and the villa wall paintings.
facts: Did you know? The 'Gypsy Girl' is really a small fragment of a larger mosaic, and some scholars argue the figure is no gypsy at all, but a maenad from the train of Dionysus, or the earth goddess Gaia. This is the largest mosaic museum in the world, and its floors were lifted out in a rescue dig before the Birecik dam filled. They are laid out following the plans of the rooms they came from, so you walk through the houses rather than over the floors.
outro: Our visit to the Zeugma Mosaic Museum ends here. Before you go, a small request: please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. These pieces have survived for centuries; let them keep their story for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
